newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rules out fish ban amid El Nino fears - adviser.
newsitem.headline: Peru rules out fish ban amid El Nino fears - adviser.

text.p: The Peruvian government has ruled out a commercial fishing ban and is committed to doing what it could to minimize the damaging effects of El Nino weather phenomenon, an adviser to the Fisheries Ministry said Friday.
"We cannot talk now of a ... ban when the quotas have not even been used," Oswaldo Hundskopf, an adviser to Fisheries Minister Carlos Boggiano Sanchez, told Reuters.

Speculation surfaced this week that Sanchez would impose a ban on fishing certain species amid fears that El Nino could drive stocks away from Peruvian waters. The rumors prompted protests from the industry, Peru's second-largest after mining.

El Nino, Spanish for "the Christ Child," is a destructive weather system that can cause drought in southern Peru and heavy rainfall in the north. It occurs every two to seven years, usually beginning near Christmas, and lasts several months.
There are signs that El Nino is starting to form, though the strength of any system that might develop has yet to be estimated.
